extracted.intended_audience: SBIR/STTR grant applicants and NIH reviewers (investigators preparing NIH human subjects/vertebrate animal and preclinical sections)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for composing NIH SBIR/STTR research application sections covering preclinical ADMET/PK, in vitro antiviral assays, in vivo mouse toxicity/efficacy studies, human subject recruitment/consent, and vertebrate animal use and statistical/power justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclinical ADMET/PK studies as go/no-go
rubrics_metrics.description: These industry-standard preclinical ADMET/PK studies will ensure that the selected analogs have the best chance to complete the drug development process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ADMET/PK data to select at least one preclinical candidate for IND-enabling studies prior to human clinical evaluation; see Commercialization Plan for detailed activities/timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cytotoxicity assay design and CC50 determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine cytotoxic properties of lead compounds in HeLa cells: untreated or treated with the compounds at ≥12 2-fold serially diluted concentrations or DMSO for 24, 48, or 72 hrs. The number of metabolically active cells will be determined using a CellTiter-Glo kit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine CC50 for each compound at each time point using non-linear regression analysis to select a non-toxic concentration range for antiviral tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vitro virus spread/egress assay design and IC50 determination
rubrics_metrics.description: To test effects on egress and spread, incubate HeLa cells with virus at MOI=0.01 for 1 hr, then overlay with medium containing compounds at ≥7 2-fold serially diluted concentrations, DMSO, or no treatment, for 24, 48, or 72 hrs. Detect infected cells with specific antibodies (EBOV GP, MARV VLP, LASV GP) and nuclei with Hoechst; photograph using an automated system and quantify virus spread with CellProfiler. Assess egress by titrating cell supernatants on Vero cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine IC50 (virus spread, egress) by non-linear regression analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity index (SI50) decision threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Use CC50/IC50 (selectivity index, SI50) to assess antiviral potential of the compounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compounds with SI50 ≥ 10 in egress assays will be tested for antiviral activity in primary human macrophages; for macrophage assays determine IC95 for use in designing animal treatment regimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vitro experimental replication and donor sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experiment, ≥3 independent tests in triplicate will be performed. Experiments with human MDMs will be performed from ≥6 different healthy adult donors (50:50 female:male ratio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect same outcome trend among donors, though magnitude may vary; analyze data for statistical significance using Student t-test for 2 groups or one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s test for >2 groups, with p ≤ 0.05 considered significant; inspect data for normality and apply transformations or non-parametric tests if deviations are seen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mouse toxicity study design and endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 4 compound candidates will be assessed for toxicity in BALB/c mice each year. Males and females randomly assigned to groups of 5 animals will receive dose formulation containing compounds at 2 different doses or vehicle PO, up to 2 times a day (BID) for 10 consecutive days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select starting dose/dosing frequency based on PK study and IC95 to maintain blood concentrations sufficient to block virus replication. Evaluate endpoints: (i) mortality; (ii) clinical signs (weight change, food consumption, decreased motor activity, eye and nasal discharge, dyspnea, unresponsiveness); (iii) serum biochemistry (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, total/direct bilirubin, urea, creatinine) at end of study; (iv) post-mortem gross examination; (v) histopathological exam of major organs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power/sample size justification for mouse toxicity studies
rubrics_metrics.description: A Student t-test (with proper data transformation if needed) will be used to compare the difference between two groups. A sample size of 5 mice/experimental condition will provide at least 80% power to detect a 3 standard deviation difference at each condition between two groups at a significance level of 0.01 (up to 5 multiple comparison adjustments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple group comparisons analyzed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey's test; p ≤ 0.05 considered significant. Experiments will be performed at least 2 times to ensure reproducibility. To evaluate sex-specific differences use both male and female groups. Planned total: 540 mice [5 mice/group × 9 treatments × 2 sexes × 2 repetitions × 3 years].

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound distribution/accumulation study design and sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Select up to 2 compounds per year to assess body distribution and accumulation over time. Collect blood and organs (liver, kidney, spleen) on days 1, 3, 5, 7, and 11. Plasma and tissues shipped to quantify compound levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether compounds (i) circulate systemically and (ii) are present at concentrations necessary to inhibit ≥95% of virus replication. Use 3 animals per time point; studies repeated at least once. Planned total: 360 mice [3 mice × 5 time points × 2 compounds × 2 sexes × 2 repetitions × 3 years].

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo treatment efficacy (mouse challenge) study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups of 10 BALB/c mice will be challenged with a lethal dose of 1,000 PFU of mouse-adapted MARV by IP. PO dosing will start 6 ± 2 hrs post-challenge and continue for 10 days at determined frequency. Animals monitored at least twice daily for signs and mortality for 21 days post-challenge. Group clinical scores recorded as the sum of all clinical observations; clinical score ≥ 12 considered terminally ill and euthanized. Three animals from each group euthanized on day 3 to collect blood and organs for virus titer (plaque assay) and load (qPCR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power calculation: to protect 70% of animals, 6–7 animals required (significance=0.05, power=0.8); account for 3 animals euthanized on day 3 so group size set to 10. Analyze viral burden by Student t-test or one-way ANOVA (Tukey); survival by Log-rank (Mantel-Cox) test; p ≤ 0.05 considered significant. Planned total: 180 mice [10 mice/group × 3 treatments × 2 sexes × 3 years].

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical score euthanasia criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: If a clinical score of ≥12 is recorded for an animal, it will be considered terminally ill and euthanized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor animals at least twice daily and record group clinical scores as the sum of observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility: Must be 18–50 years old; must weigh at least 110 pounds; cannot be pregnant; cannot be on a medication; no illness within 10 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special groups (pregnant females, fetuses, the elderly, children, prisoners and the cognitively impaired, etc.) will be excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects inclusion of women and minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be no discrimination based on gender, race, or ethnicity. Recruitment directed at acquiring approximately 50% females and 50% males. Women who are currently pregnant will be excluded. Recruitment monitored to assure minority representation, target percentages based on San Antonio demographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If usual methods yield only Caucasian volunteers, broaden notices/locations and explicitly encourage women and minority students to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and retention practices for human subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit subjects from healthy lab and office personnel, Texas Biomed employees, students at local colleges/universities, hospitals, and the community using flyers and community events. Monitor recruitment to assure minority representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention: subjects allowed to donate no more than 480 ml blood in an 8-week span; may participate multiple times as long as donation limit observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent and confidentiality protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain written informed consent after explaining risks and allowing questions; subject free to withdraw at any time. Specimens and data labeled with a numerical code; subject names not appear on specimens; date/amount recorded in a locked notebook accessible only to lab personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain potential risks (needle pain, bruising, lightheadedness, rare fainting); venipuncture performed by physician or qualified technician using sterile technique; use antecubital vein, sitting/supine position, apply firm pressure after draw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects risk minimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Protections to minimize risks include qualified personnel performing venipuncture, sterile technique, position control, pressure after withdrawal, limitation of blood volume per subject, and de-identification of specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usual amount of blood 30–200 ml; any single adult limited to a maximum of 480 ml in any two-month period. No incidental findings expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of vulnerable populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Special groups (pregnant females, fetuses, the elderly, children, prisoners and the cognitively impaired, etc.) will be excluded from this protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale provided for excluding children and aged adults (additional risks, anatomical/physiologic concerns) and plan to study adults first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animal specifications and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Use wild-type BALB/c mice (supplied by The Jackson Laboratory) for in vivo toxicity, concentration/accumulation studies, and infections. BALB/c chosen because they are susceptible to mouse-adapted Marburg virus and develop symptoms consistent with human infection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 4–5 week old mice; use 50:50 female:male ratio to avoid confounding by sex differences. Experimental needs enumerate specific animal counts and study endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and safety monitoring plan items
rubrics_metrics.description: Section requests Data and Safety Monitoring Plan and whether a Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) will be appointed for this study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this study DSMB will not be appointed; overall structure of study team and monitoring plan must be described in application.
